propositions: Re-cloning the tracker without preserving git-ignored local state (.env-id, .opcert-key, .opcert-key.pub) silently regenerates a new environment identity, invalidating all prior attestations signed by the old principal.
Minting a fresh .env-id when the store already contains events from a different environment produces no warning or signal, allowing operators to orphan attestations unaware.
The old environment's op-cert public key is never committed and becomes unrecoverable after re-clone, making foreign attestations permanently unverifiable even with an accept-list.

A re-clone or multi-clone environment must warn loudly with an explicit REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY override rather than refuse outright, because second clones mounting a shared branch legitimately need their own identity.

rebar fsck must emit a counted ENV_ID_MISMATCH check scoped by author to detect when the current environment's own author wrote events under a different env-id, signaling re-clone or per-author machine moves.
